about: 30 named visual techniques. Names and the four jobs are Jason Murray's public labels (Short 2BYgOxYTE-0, 2026-09-24; newsletter MAD 011; Shorts to 2026-10-19). job_src 'map' = line colour read off his public map; 'ours' = placed by us. def_src names his source, or 'ours' for our own definition. conf 'low' = name read from 4-pixel letters. menu = the heading of his Art Direction Menu it serves, placed by us. Built 2026-10-20; nothing here comes from the Iris app.

jobs.differentiate: Make one thing stand apart from the rest
jobs.group: Make separate things read as one
jobs.sequence: Set the order the eye reads in
jobs.predict: Set up an expectation and use it

techniques.name: Scale disparity
techniques.def: utilizes the contrast of sizes in order to accentuate a message
techniques.look: Two things at sizes they never are together

techniques.name: Saturation blocking
techniques.def: Large flat fields of saturated colour that cut the subject out of its ground
techniques.look: Hard-edged blocks of one strong colour

techniques.name: Simultaneous contrast
techniques.def: A colour or tone made to read stronger by what sits next to it
techniques.look: A hue that looks louder than it is because of its neighbour

techniques.name: Warm and cool split
techniques.def: Warm against cool light or colour to split subject from setting
techniques.look: Orange subject, blue surround, or the reverse

techniques.name: Semantic juxtaposition
techniques.def: Two things that mean opposite things set side by side so the gap makes the point
techniques.look: A pairing that should not belong together

techniques.name: Isolation in void
techniques.def: Remove the distractions and surround your subject with empty space
techniques.look: One subject in a large empty field

techniques.name: Figure-ground reversal
techniques.def: the positive and negative spaces in an image can both read as the subject
techniques.look: The empty shape between things forms a second subject

techniques.name: Symmetry
techniques.def: Mirror balance that makes the frame read as one ordered whole
techniques.look: A centre axis with matching halves

techniques.name: Face schema
techniques.def: An arrangement the eye reads as a face: two points over a line
techniques.look: A face hiding in objects, type or architecture

techniques.name: Visual rhyme
techniques.def: A shape, colour or line repeated across different things so they read as related
techniques.look: The same curve or colour echoed in two unlike objects

techniques.name: Anthropomorphism
techniques.def: Giving an object or animal a human posture, expression or role
techniques.look: A product or animal acting like a person

techniques.name: Semantic compounding
techniques.def: Two ideas fused into one object so the image carries both meanings
techniques.look: A hybrid object that is two things at once

techniques.name: Common region
techniques.def: Things inside one boundary read as one group
techniques.look: A box, panel or shape holding several items

techniques.name: Good continuation
techniques.def: The eye follows a smooth line or curve through separate elements
techniques.look: Separate parts aligned on one unbroken path

techniques.name: Center placement
techniques.def: The subject dead centre, read first and held there
techniques.look: Subject on the centre point with calm around it

techniques.name: Leading lines
techniques.def: Lines in the scene that run toward the subject
techniques.look: Roads, rails, edges converging on one point

techniques.name: Gaze cue
techniques.def: the direction someone is looking suggests where we should look
techniques.look: A person looking at the product or the line

techniques.name: Size hierarchy
techniques.def: Sizes set the reading order, biggest first
techniques.look: One dominant element, then smaller ones in rank

techniques.name: Frame within a frame
techniques.def: turns the portrait into a small stage. Scenes within scenes.
techniques.look: A doorway, box or window holding the subject

techniques.name: Body vector
techniques.def: A pose, limb or movement that points the eye onward
techniques.look: An arm, leg or lean aimed at something

techniques.name: Reading path
techniques.def: A planned route through the frame, usually a Z or an S
techniques.look: Elements placed so the eye zigzags in order

techniques.name: Closure
techniques.def: Leave a shape incomplete so the viewer completes it
techniques.look: A broken outline the mind still reads whole

techniques.name: Forced perspective
techniques.def: Distance used to make sizes lie, so near and far things interact
techniques.look: A hand that seems to hold a far building

techniques.name: Caricatural exaggeration
techniques.def: One feature pushed past real proportion so it carries the message
techniques.look: An oversized head, hand or product

techniques.name: Form substitution
techniques.def: Use the shape of one thing to mean something else
techniques.look: A familiar silhouette made of something else

techniques.name: Visual quotation
techniques.def: references known genres, periods, or pieces of work
techniques.look: A known painting, film or genre restaged

techniques.name: Pattern break
techniques.def: establish a repeating pattern and then interrupt it
techniques.look: One item out of step in a repeated row

techniques.name: Occlusion
techniques.def: Something partly hidden so the viewer infers the rest and leans in
techniques.look: A face or product half behind something

techniques.name: Crop at the edge
techniques.def: The frame cuts the subject, implying more beyond the edge
techniques.look: A subject cut hard by the border

techniques.name: Visible facture
techniques.def: when the process can be seen in the final work
techniques.look: Brushwork, grain, seams or built scenery left visible
